candidates.reasoning: C48 was the strongest gap candidate and was probed hardest (7 searches). The kintsugi 'fracture-to-feature' inversion (reinforce, don't regularize-away, the interference/failure boundary) is genuinely the most distinctive of the eight. Two reformulations initially returned only interference-AVOIDANCE work (MER/InfLoRA/EWC) and the 'scar tissue' framing returned zero ML hits — which momentarily looked like a possible narrow gap. BUT reformulation 5 produced a forced functional hit on the CORE claim: 'Continual Learning with Synthetic Boundary Experience Blending' explicitly ENRICHES the feature space near decision boundaries for robust continual learning, and DyART reinforces vulnerable boundary points. Brain-inspired feature exaggeration also amplifies at interference points. Therefore the core effect is published. R14 applied honestly in BOTH directions: I did not explain away the gap prematurely (probed 7x), but the boundary-enrichment collision is real and direct, so the verdict is COLLISION, not GAP. The kintsugi-specific 'encode learning history in the reinforced boundary' narrative is an arbitrary extra narrative, not a separately-defensible mechanism -> narrow_version_nontrivial=false. Composite slightly higher (36) than the others to reflect that this one is the least-thoroughly-anticipated framing, but still below any gap threshold.
